_about: Patterns that identify an owner entry as anonymous or generic rather than a named party. Configurable: institutions whose records use other conventions should add their own patterns rather than editing rule code.
_why: An anonymous entry is unremarkable in most of a collection's history. Inside the persecution band it is the standard way an interrupted ownership history reads once a name has dropped out, so the rule is deliberately scoped to that band rather than flagging anonymity everywhere.
_matching: Patterns are matched case- and accent-insensitively on word boundaries against `owner_name` and each of `owner_name_variants`. They are substrings, not whole-value equality: 'private collection, Switzerland' matches the pattern 'private collection'.
_band_note: The band for this rule is 1933-01-01 to 1950-12-31, as specified in the project methodology notes. It is deliberately NARROWER than the persecution-onset table's risk band (which runs to 1955) and is not keyed to territory: anonymity is a property of the record, not of a place.

band.source: Project methodology notes, Heuristic Layer rule 7 ('specifically within the 1933-1950 range').
